hint: Look for a choice broad enough to cover both access and the added result.
explanation: The passage centers on how a neighborhood archive lets residents preserve oral histories and also leads to recorded interviews and digitized photographs.
solutionSteps: Identify the project introduced in the passage.
Note both what residents can do and the additional result.
Choose the option that matches the requested detail or includes both central points without adding a claim.
strategy: Summarize each sentence in a few words, then combine only the recurring ideas.
trap: A choice may repeat a vivid detail but distort its role or make it the entire main idea.
principles: A main idea must cover the passage as a whole; a detail must be explicitly stated.
choices: Yarrow Harbor ended the project after a one-day trial.
Only trained professionals were allowed to use a neighborhood archive.
recorded interviews and digitized photographs was the project's only stated goal.

distractorRationales.reason: The text says the project became or remains active, not that it ended.
The passage describes resident participation and never limits access to professionals.
The result is an outcome, while the project also gives residents a way to participate.

stimulus.content: Near Alder Point, beside a bicycle repair stand, Gavin Reed usually recorded about 25 coastal grasses during each survey. On three surveys after shallow water collected among the plots, the count rose to an average of 38. Surveys without that condition remained near 25.

stem: Which conclusion is best supported by the text?
hint: Prefer a cautious conclusion that reflects the observed association without claiming causation.
explanation: Counts were consistently higher after shallow water collected among the plots, so the condition may affect observations; the data do not establish a permanent change or a cause.
solutionSteps: Compare the usual count of 25 with the conditional average of 38.
Notice that the count changes alongside one condition.
Select the qualified conclusion and reject absolute or causal claims.
strategy: Match the strength of the conclusion to the strength of the evidence.
trap: Words such as “always,” “only,” and “caused” make a choice stronger than correlational evidence permits.
principles: An observed association supports a cautious inference, not automatic causation.
choices: The condition permanently doubled the population of coastal grasses.
The stated condition may influence how many coastal grasses are observed.
coastal grasses can be observed only under the stated condition.
The survey method caused the stated condition to occur.

distractorRationales.reason: The observation counts rose temporarily and did not double; population size was not measured.
The researcher observed about 25 even without the condition.
The passage reports an association and gives no evidence that surveying caused the condition.

hint: Prefer a cautious conclusion that reflects the observed association without claiming causation.
explanation: Counts were consistently higher after shallow water collected among the plots, so the condition may affect observations; the data do not establish a permanent change or a cause.
solutionSteps: Compare the usual count of 23 with the conditional average of 32.
Notice that the count changes alongside one condition.
Select the qualified conclusion and reject absolute or causal claims.
strategy: Match the strength of the conclusion to the strength of the evidence.
trap: Words such as “always,” “only,” and “caused” make a choice stronger than correlational evidence permits.
principles: An observed association supports a cautious inference, not automatic causation.
choices: The stated condition may influence how many lichen patches are observed.
The condition permanently doubled the population of lichen patches.
lichen patches can be observed only under the stated condition.
The survey method caused the stated condition to occur.

distractorRationales.reason: The observation counts rose temporarily and did not double; population size was not measured.
The researcher observed about 23 even without the condition.
